en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Donkey.
2. The Question on the Cock “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘five qualities of a cock should be adopted’—which are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a cock retires into solitude at the proper time and on the proper occasion;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should, at the proper time and on the proper occasion,
sweep the courtyard of the shrine, set out drinking water and water for washing, attend to his body, bathe, pay homage to the shrine,
go to see the elder bhikkhus, and then, at the proper time and on the proper occasion, enter an empty dwelling.
This, great king, is the first quality of the cock that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, the cock rises at the proper time;
even so, great king, the practitioner of yoga, having risen at the proper time, [should go] to the shrine courtyard.
Having swept [the dwelling], having set out drinking water and water for washing, having attended to the body, and having paid homage to the shrine,
one should enter an empty dwelling once again. This, Great King,
is the second quality of the cock that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, just as a cock, having pecked and pecked at the earth, swallows its food, even so, Great King,
should a practitioner of yoga, having reflected and reflected,
swallow his food: "Neither for sport, nor for intoxication, nor for adornment, nor for embellishment, but only for this..."
‘For the maintenance of this body, for its sustenance, for the allaying of hunger, and for the support of the holy life:
thus I shall eliminate old feelings and not give rise to new feelings, and there will be for me health, blamelessness, and a comfortable dwelling.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the cock that should be adopted.
This was also said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God beyond gods:
“Like the flesh of one’s own son in the wilderness,
or like oil for the axle of a cart;”
"Thus he takes his food,
not being infatuated, for the sake of maintenance.
Furthermore, Great King, even though a cock has eyes, it is blind at night.
In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga, though not blind, should act as if he were blind;

even while wandering for alms in the forest or in the village, he should act like one who is blind, deaf, and mute toward objects that provoke passion—whether forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or tactile sensations.
He should not grasp at their signs, nor should he grasp at their secondary characteristics.
This, great king, is the fourth quality of the cock that should be adopted.
And this was said, great king, by the Elder Mahākaccāyana:
"As one with sight [regards] the blind..."
Like one who has ears but is deaf;
like one who has wisdom but is mute;
like one who is strong but is weak.
"When one's own welfare has arisen,
one should lie down like a dead snake.
Furthermore, Great King, even when being pelted with clods of earth, sticks, clubs, and mallets, a cock does not abandon its own home.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner, a follower of yoga, whether performing robe-making, or new construction work, or carrying out the duties and counter-duties, or giving instruction, or receiving instruction, must not abandon wise attention (*yoniso manasikāra*).
For this, Great King, is the home of the practitioner: namely, wise attention.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the cock that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was said by the Blessed One, the God above Gods: “And what, monks, is a monk’s own range, his ancestral domain?
It is these four foundations of mindfulness.”
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Sāriputta,
the General of the Dhamma: "Just as a well-tamed elephant does not crush its own trunk;”
One discerns what is edible and what is inedible for the sake of maintaining one's own livelihood;
even so should it be by a son of the Buddha.
Or rather, by one who is heedful,
the word of the Victor should not be trampled upon;
it is the most excellent of mental applications.
The second question: On the Cock’s Foot.
